# QuilrAI Documentation

> QuilrAI provides an LLM Gateway, MCP Gateway, Network monitoring and Process mapping for securing, controlling, and optimizing AI application traffic.

## Platform Features

- [Token Saving](https://docs.quilrai.dev/token-saving.md): Cross-product guide to reducing LLM prompt and MCP agent-context tokens with JSON compression, HTML/Markdown to text, text compression, and OneMCP smart tool search.

## LLM Gateway

Connect to LLM providers and SDK-style guardrail integrations - OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Oracle OCI, and Copilot Studio - through a single API key. QuilrAI can infer providers from the requested model, or route traffic through routing groups for weighted load balancing, model-level routing, and automatic failover with zero code changes in your application.

- [Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/quick-start.md): Set up the LLM Gateway in 4 steps - create an app, add a provider key, configure guardrails, and connect your application.
- [Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/architecture.md): Request processing pipeline - Validate, Scan, Transform, Route - with a visual diagram of every stage.
- [Integration Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/integration-guide.md): Endpoint URLs, authentication setup, and code examples for connecting your app to the gateway, including OpenAI-compatible access to Bedrock Converse, Vertex AI Gemini, and Anthropic Messages models, boto3 Bedrock Runtime, and Copilot Studio.
- [LLM Gateway Log Export API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/log-export-api.md): Export single-key or all-apps LLM Gateway request logs as newline-delimited JSON with cursor pagination, a 15-minute export lag, and a 15-day retention window.
- [Provider Support](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/provider-support.md): Supported LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Oracle OCI, Copilot Studio) and their capability matrix, including Oracle gateway sign-in and provider-native models through OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- [Unified Completions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/unified-completions.md): Compatibility details for OpenAI Chat Completions requests translated to provider-native APIs such as Bedrock Converse, Vertex AI Gemini generateContent, and Anthropic Messages, including parameters, messages, tools, structured output, streaming, and unsupported features.
- [AWS Bedrock boto3 Runtime](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/bedrock-boto3.md): Use boto3 Bedrock Runtime with QuilrAI by setting endpoint_url, with Converse, ConverseStream, and InvokeModel coverage.
- [AWS Bedrock Assume Role Setup](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/bedrock-assume-role.md): Configure Bedrock provider keys with cross-account IAM role assumption instead of long-lived AWS credentials.
- [Oracle OCI Gateway Sign-In Setup](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/oracle-cross-tenancy.md): Grant QuilrAI cross-tenancy access to OCI Generative AI for Chat Completions and Responses without sharing an Oracle API key or signing key.
- [HA & SLA](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/ha-and-sla.md): Regional endpoints, recommended retry strategy, connection pooling, and 99.6% uptime SLA.
- [UX Changelog](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/ux-changelog.md): Recent interface improvements - tagging, filtering, and quality-of-life updates.

### LLM Gateway Features

- [Request Routing](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/request-routing.md): Automatic provider inference from requested models, plus routing groups for weight-based load balancing, model-level routing, and failover across multiple providers and models behind a single API key.
- [Token Saving](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/token-saving.md): Reduce input token usage with JSON compression, HTML/Markdown to text, and text compression.
- [Guardian Agent](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/guardian-agent.md): Gateway-side policy checks for dependency safety and task adherence.
- [Security Guardrails](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/security-guardrails.md): Detect and act on PII, PHI, PCI, financial data, and adversarial inputs in requests and responses.
- [Custom Intents](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/custom-intents.md): Define your own detection categories trained with positive and negative examples.
- [Rate Limits](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/rate-limits.md): Control request rates, token budgets, and API key expiration.
- [Prompt Store](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/prompt-store.md): Manage and version system prompts centrally; reference one or more from a single request, mix in inline instructions, and substitute template variables.
- [Red Team Testing](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/red-team-testing.md): Benchmark the model behind an app against fixed adversarial and capability suites. Covers simulating your app with a system prompt and tool schemas, the Guardian counterfactual, and compliance framework rollups.
- [Reading the Report](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/red-team-report.md): Interpret a completed red team run. What the headline pass rate counts and excludes, automated versus reviewed verdicts, per-suite results, Guardian residual failures and over-blocks, framework rollups, the knowledge horizon, and what makes two runs comparable.
- [Agentic Red Teaming](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/agentic-red-teaming.md): Multi-turn adversarial assessment of a live AI agent; connect an HTTP/API agent or a model provider (OpenAI/Azure/Anthropic/Gemini/Bedrock), with the API integration contract and remediation output.
- [Identity Aware](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/identity-aware.md): Authenticate and track individual users behind each API key via JWT/JWKS or header validation.
- [SDK Mode](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/sdk-mode.md): Scan content directly from your application code with no LLM proxy required.
- [Copilot Studio](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/copilot-studio.md): Connect Microsoft Copilot Studio external threat detection to QuilrAI guardrails before tool execution.
- [Agent Monitoring](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/agent-monitoring.md): Correlate gateway LLM calls with agent runs, traces, workflows, and conversations via W3C/vendor tracing headers, Quilr agent headers, baggage, or provider request-body metadata.
- [Self-Service Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/self-service/overview.md): How self-service gives developers gateway access without an admin minting each key - shared parent key vs named user API keys, the `sk-quilr-…:ss1.…` key format, the five access capabilities, and the portal's Settings, Logs, and Findings tabs.
- [Self-Service Admin Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/self-service/admin-guide.md): For QuilrAI platform admins - choose a credential mode, grant Viewer Access, Settings Request Access, Direct Settings Update, API Key Visibility, and All Logs Visibility, scope each with Everyone/Specific rules, smart groups, and exceptions, review change requests, and revoke access.
- [Self-Service Developer Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway/features/self-service/developer-guide.md): For developers - sign in to the Self-Service portal, read the app cards, create and revoke named user API keys, call the gateway with them, view your own logs and findings, submit settings change requests for admin approval, and a tour of the settings editor sections (security guardrails, additional guardrails, Guardian Agent, token saving).

## Playground

- [LLM Gateway Playground](https://docs.quilrai.dev/llm-gateway-playground): Full-page, console-style studio that fires real LLM Gateway requests from the browser against any gateway base URL. Streams chat completions live and runs every surface - chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, classic completions, embeddings, rerank, and text to speech - plus `quilr_sdk` guardrail checks against `POST /sdk/v1/check` and a Log Export surface that pages the LLM or MCP Gateway log export API (with an `sk-export-` key) into an Excel-ready CSV. Generates the exact cURL, Python, and JavaScript for each request.

## MCP Gateway

## Quilr-Provided MCPs

- [Quilr-Provided MCPs](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/overview.md): Compare Quilr-built and operated MCP integrations by use case, capabilities, connection method, and whether their tool surface can change provider data.
- [Official MCP Comparison](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/official-comparison.md): Provider-by-provider comparison of official MCP or API coverage with Quilr's custom tool surface, operating model, safety controls, compound tools, and known limits.
- [Microsoft 365 v3](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/microsoft-365-v3.md): Flagship unified Microsoft 365 MCP for Outlook mail and calendar, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, directory, OneNote, cross-workload search, batch operations, and delta sync, including a capability comparison with ChatGPT Outlook and SharePoint connectors.
- [SharePoint](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/sharepoint.md): Six consolidated tools for SharePoint sites, drives, files, folders, lists, list items, URL resolution, controlled writes, and confirmed deletes.
- [Excel](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/excel.md): Eight workbook dispatchers covering worksheets, ranges, formulas, formatting, tables, named ranges, charts, pivots, and function evaluation.
- [Microsoft Tasks & Planner](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/microsoft-tasks-planner.md): Focused Microsoft To Do and Planner tools for personal tasks, plans, buckets, and team tasks.
- [Azure DevOps Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/azure-devops.md): Centrally hosted Azure DevOps MCP with compatibility dispatchers, direct tools, compound engineering intelligence, multi-organization selection, and confirmed destructive operations.
- [Jira](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/jira.md): Compact ten-tool Jira surface for projects, issue retrieval and search, creation, assignment, transitions, and comments.
- [Confluence](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/confluence.md): Nine-tool Confluence surface for spaces, pages, CQL search, page creation and updates, and comments with no destructive tools.
- [Google Workspace](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/google-workspace.md): Combined Gmail, Calendar, and Drive MCP with thirteen tools, customer-owned OAuth, shared-drive discovery, and file export.
- [Figma](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/figma.md): Nineteen API-oriented Figma tools for design context, variables, screenshots, libraries, comments, assets, and Code Connect administration.
- [Calendly](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/calendly.md): Forty scheduling tools with a customer-owned, pre-registered OAuth application alternative to Calendly's DCR-only official MCP.
- [HubSpot CRM](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/hubspot.md): Nine consolidated tools for CRM search, batch reads, associations, schemas, owners, records, notes, tasks, and controlled archive.
- [Avoma](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/avoma.md): Four read-only meeting-intelligence tools for meeting details, transcripts, and structured notes.
- [Writer](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/writer.md): Hosted ten-tool Writer surface for chat, applications, Knowledge Graphs, files, translation, vision, and web search.
- [Optimizely Experimentation](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/optimizely.md): Quilr-built experimentation MCP for schema-guided queries, reporting, entity lifecycle, exports, audit history, collaborators, and datafiles.
- [Semrush Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/semrush.md): Twenty-three explicit SEO and market-intelligence tools with compound domain and keyword briefs, comparisons, gaps, projects, and quota visibility.
- [BrowserStack Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/browserstack.md): Forty-eight tools for Automate, App Automate, diagnostics, screenshots, deep Test Management, and controlled bulk operations.
- [Athenahealth](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/athenahealth.md): Safety-first athenaOne and FHIR MCP with capability packs, allowlists, idempotent confirmed writes, separately enabled deletes, bulk exports, and PHI-safe telemetry.
- [Tavily](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/tavily.md): Eight read-only tools for search, extraction, site mapping, crawling, asynchronous research, usage, and key information.
- [Cycode](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/cycode.md): Remotely operated Cycode CLI MCP wrapper for service status and secret scanning without general shell access.
- [Quilr Web Search](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/web-search.md): Minimal two-tool web search and webpage retrieval integration with optional gateway domain policy.
- [SketchIt](https://docs.quilrai.dev/quilr-provided-mcps/sketchit.md): Decision guide comparing the credential-free SketchIt diagram and chart renderer to the self-hosted, editable Excalidraw canvas.

## MCP Gateway

- [Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/quick-start.md): Set up the MCP Gateway in 4 steps - add an MCP, configure tools and guardrails, connect an agent, and monitor.
- [Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/architecture.md): Tool call processing pipeline - Authenticate, Authorize, Scan, Policy, Connect - with auth mediation details.
- [Integration Guide](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/integration-guide.md): MCP endpoint URLs, client-to-gateway authentication, gateway-to-upstream auth modes, user claims forwarding, and connection examples.
- [OneMCP](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/onemcp.md): Unified OneMCP endpoint, smart discovery tools, native memory tools, and inline authentication through an in-chat connector card or connection-link fallback.
- [Agent Custom Instructions](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/agent-instructions.md): Copy-paste custom-instruction text that steers Claude, ChatGPT, and GitHub Copilot to use the OneMCP discovery flow (find_relevant_tools, call_tool, list_mcp_connections), with per-client placement and org-level admin push options and scope caveats.
- [MCP Provider Setup](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/overview.md): Provider-specific setup for MCP servers that need manual connection - when to create an OAuth app vs. add a provider-generated URL, prerequisites, and secret handling.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Slack](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/slack.md): Create a Slack app, enable Model Context Protocol, add the redirect URL and user-token scopes, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [MCP Provider Setup: GitHub](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/github.md): Create a GitHub OAuth app, set the callback URL, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Zoho](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/zoho.md): Connect Zoho Cliq MCP - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; generate the MCP server URL in the Zoho MCP console and add it manually.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Google Workspace](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/google-workspace.md): Connect the QuilrAI-built Google Workspace MCP for Gmail, Calendar, and Drive - create a Google Cloud OAuth client, enable all three APIs, add the required scopes including openid and Drive read access, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Figma](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/figma.md): Connect the QuilrAI-built Figma MCP (design context, comments, Code Connect) - create a Figma OAuth app, add the redirect URI and required scopes, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret for manual OAuth.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Datadog](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/datadog.md): Connect Datadog MCP - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; register the QuilrAI callback URL in Datadog Organization Settings under MCP OAuth Redirect URLs, enable MCP Access and the separate MCP Write Access opt-in, pick the core or toolsets=all endpoint for your Datadog site, and add that endpoint URL manually.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Calendly Custom](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/calendly.md): Create a customer-owned Calendly OAuth app, configure the QuilrAI callback URL and least-privilege scopes, add the QuilrAI-built custom Calendly MCP with its Client ID and Client Secret, connect users, test tools, and handle rotation or reconnection.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Azure DevOps Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/azure-devops.md): Register or approve a Microsoft Entra delegated OAuth application, connect the QuilrAI-built Azure DevOps MCP, resolve one or multiple organizations safely, review all 47 tools and their purposes, test read-only workflows, and troubleshoot consent, scope, or reconnection issues.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Semrush Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/semrush.md): Connect the QuilrAI-built Semrush Advanced MCP with a Semrush API key, configure credential ownership and placement, verify read-only and batch research, and troubleshoot API access and unit usage.
- [MCP Provider Setup: BrowserStack Advanced](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/browserstack.md): Connect the QuilrAI-built BrowserStack Advanced MCP with a username and access key, use the raw or optional Base64 composite credential format, verify read-only and batch tools, and troubleshoot permissions and rotation.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Excalidraw](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/excalidraw.md): Connect Excalidraw - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; self-host the community Excalidraw MCP server with its live canvas, bridge stdio to streamable HTTP with Supergateway, and add the resulting /mcp URL manually. Covers all 26 tools, environment variables, and network-security guidance.
- [MCP Provider Setup: Asana](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/asana.md): Connect the Asana V2 MCP server (https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp) - create an Asana MCP app in the developer console, add the QuilrAI redirect URL, configure workspace distribution, and paste the Client ID and Client Secret into QuilrAI with Auto-detect auth mode. Covers the retired V1 /sse endpoint and workspace-distribution errors.
- [MCP Provider Setup: SketchIt](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/sketchit.md): Enable the credential-free SketchIt diagram and chart renderer, verify rendering and the inline design/variation flow, use it effectively, and troubleshoot validation, capacity, and icon-assignment errors.
- [MCP Provider Setup: dbt Labs](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/mcp-provider-setup/dbt-labs.md): Connect the dbt platform remote MCP server - no OAuth app or Client ID/Secret needed; copy the account-specific MCP Endpoint URL from dbt Account settings > Access URLs, add it manually, and authorize through dbt sign-in plus MFA enrollment. Covers the token-based alternative with Authorization and x-dbt-* headers, PAT vs service token limits, toolset restriction headers, and the remote toolsets (Semantic Layer, Discovery, SQL, Administrative API, Fusion, Product Docs).
- [MCP Gateway Log Export API](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/log-export-api.md): Export backend-scoped or tenant-scoped MCP tool call logs as newline-delimited JSON with cursor pagination, a 15-minute export lag, and a 15-day retention window.

### MCP Gateway Features

- [MCP Library](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/mcp-library.md): One-click install pre-built MCP integrations from the catalog across productivity, developer tools, and more.
- [Tools Management](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/tools-management.md): Control which MCP tools are available to agents, organized by risk level (read, write, destructive).
- [Agents Configuration](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/agents-configuration.md): Map AI agents to MCPs, manage per-agent permissions, and monitor usage statistics.
- [Security Guardrails](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/security-guardrails.md): Detect sensitive data (PII, PHI, PCI) and adversarial attacks in MCP tool call inputs and outputs.
- [Access Control](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/access-control.md): Restrict which AI agents can use each MCP server via User-Agent header matching.
- [API Tokens](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/api-tokens.md): Generate and manage Bearer tokens scoped to specific agents for programmatic MCP access, and understand how static upstream API keys are injected separately.
- [OAuth Connect](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/oauth-connect.md): Authorize OAuth-protected MCP servers with Dynamic Client Registration, manual credentials, OAuth passthrough, or OneMCP's in-chat connector card and connection-link fallbacks.
- [Web Search Policy](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/web-search-policy.md): Filter web search domains using enterprise security gateway rules (Zscaler ZIA, Prisma Access, FortiGate, Cisco Umbrella).
- [Token Saving](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/token-saving.md): Reduce MCP discovery and tool-output token usage with OneMCP smart tool search plus per-MCP JSON compression, HTML/Markdown to text, and text compression.
- [User Claims Forwarding](https://docs.quilrai.dev/mcp-gateway/features/user-claims-forwarding.md): Forward gateway-generated, versioned user identity to trusted non-OAuth MCP backends in the reserved X-User-Claims header for direct MCP and OneMCP traffic.

## Compliance API Integration

### Claude

- [Overview](https://docs.quilrai.dev/compliance-api-integration/claude/overview.md): Connect to Anthropic's Compliance API to monitor Claude.ai usage - sync organizations, users, chats, projects, and activities, with automatic DLP scanning of all user inputs.
- [Key Management](https://docs.quilrai.dev/compliance-api-integration/claude/key-management.md): Register, monitor, and revoke Compliance API keys - keys are validated on registration, stored encrypted, and drive continuous sync and DLP passes.

## Endpoint Agent

- [Network Monitoring Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/network-monitoring/quick-start.md): Set up Network Monitoring in 4 steps - install the Sentinel agent, enable traffic interception, configure DLP policies, and monitor activity.
- [Network Monitoring Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/network-monitoring/architecture.md): Request processing pipeline - Intercept, Inspect, Scan, Enforce - with TLS MITM, DLP engine, and health monitoring.
- [Process Mapping Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/process-mapping/quick-start.md): Set up Process Mapping in 4 steps - deploy the System Monitor, review discovered applications, configure policies, and monitor activity.
- [Process Mapping Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/process-mapping/architecture.md): Discovery and enforcement pipeline - Discover, Correlate, Sync, Enforce - covering process monitoring, Lua-based AI agent scanning, and governance.
- [Backend Integration Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/be/quick-start.md): Set up backend sync in 4 steps - configure connection, verify discovery, confirm governance pull, and check activity reporting.
- [Backend Integration Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/be/architecture.md): Synchronization architecture - how the agent communicates with the Quilr backend via polling and event-driven reports, with local persistence and reliability layers.
- [Requisites Quick Start](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/requisites/quick-start.md): Verify endpoint readiness in 4 steps - check OS support, access rights, network requirements, and platform-specific drivers.
- [Requisites Architecture](https://docs.quilrai.dev/endpoint-agent/requisites/architecture.md): Platform dependency map - how the agent's core, network monitor, and certificate management interact with macOS and Windows system internals.
